title: A mobile robotic chemist
summary: A mobile robot ran 688 experiments in eight days in a ten-variable space, guided by a batch Bayesian algorithm, to search for photocatalysts that produce hydrogen from water; the best mixtures were six times more active than the initial formulations. This optimizes a formulation, not a new structure; only the abstract was reviewed.
ai_technology: Batch Bayesian optimization and mobile robot

evidence.tested: 688 autonomous experiments over eight days in a ten-variable space; the best photocatalyst mixtures were about six times more active than the initial formulations.
evidence.unknown: The abstract lists no limitations of this study; it notes that atomistic simulations cannot yet capture multi-scale complexity and that robots are hard to adopt widely across diverse samples and instruments.
evidence.ai_role: A batch Bayesian algorithm chose which experiments the mobile robot ran next, automating the researcher rather than the instruments.
